Hi Maya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our conversation I attached three compact scenarios for an SLA uplift (uptime tiers, response windows, and an optional escalation retainer) so your architects and procurement can model the economics. Quick notes up front:

- Scenario A: 99.9% uptime, 4h P1 response, regional oncall coverage (no retainer). Small per-token uplift.
- Scenario B: 99.95% uptime, 1h P1 response, 24/7 oncall (with on-call retainer). Mid uplift + guaranteed escalation lanes.
- Scenario C: 99.99% uptime, 30m P1 response, priority engineers + dedicated success manager (commitment required). Highest uplift, includes quarterly runbooks and two scheduled DR tests/year.

Attachments: SLA-Uplift-Scenarios.xlsx (pricing tabs + assumptions), Ops-Oncall-Routing.drawio (proposed pager routing).

Two asks: can procurement review the Scenario B table and confirm whether a quarterly retainer fits your billing cadence? And can we lock a 45-minute follow-up on Monday to walk the engineering team through the routing diagram? I’m free Mon 10:30–12:00 PT.

Warmly,

Maya—

Thanks for the questions. Some quick clarifications (summary first, then brief mechanics):

Summary:
- Retainer billing: monthly by default, with an option for quarterly invoicing if you commit to a 12-month retainer. Unused retainer hours do not roll forward; instead we offer a monthly rollover credit in the first two months of an annual commitment.
- Escalation path: Scenario B routes to a Redwood priority queue (shared priority engineers) for initial triage; we include an automatic 1-hour escalation to your dedicated account engineer for P1s during business-hours. Scenario C places you on a dedicated rotation with named engineers.
- Credit calc: For partial-hour outages we use a laddered credit schedule tied to incident severity and duration (examples in the attached spreadsheet). Credits are applied against the next invoice; in the case of Dedicated customers we can also apply a one-time usage credit if approved by finance.

Mechanics / Follow-up items:
- Procurement asks: if quarterly invoicing is required, we need billing contact + PO cadence.
- Ops asks: we recommend a 30-minute run-through of the drawio routing to ensure we map your existing pager and on-call layers into our escalation policies (avoid double-escalation).

Draft agenda for Monday (45m):
1) 5m — goals and decision criteria (Maya)
2) 15m — walkthrough of Scenario B (pricing, retainer model) (Laura)
3) 15m — ops routing diagram and escalation playbook (Jonas/Aditya)
4) 10m — procurement/next steps and DocuSign timeline (Jonas)

If that works I’ll send a calendar invite and attach a slightly annotated spreadsheet that flags assumptions we made about traffic and failure modes.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
